Institutional capacities, mechanisms and policies enhanced to provide access to justice and protect human rights for all, especially those at risk of being left behind in compliance with international human rights standards.
children.description:
Agencies: UNDP, UNODC, UNHCR, IOM, UNICEF																		
UNHCR through advocacy interventions and promotional events contributed to advance Institutional capacities. UNHCR  with the support of the partner and Ombudsperson Institution has organized high-level event with an aim to raise the awareness of the authorities on challenges and obstacles persons of concern face in addressing their requests for late birth registration, resulting with the authorities pledge to create a systemic mechanism for identification, prevention, reduction, and protection of unregistered persons at risk of statelessness. Extensive advocacies yield the results in authorities’ considerations for inclusion of the identified gaps and challenges into concept documents providing basis for the revision of laws for citizenship and civil status. 
Apart from daily advocacy interventions UNHCR has produced retorts and presented them in different events aiming at advancing the implementation and the protection of the rights of non-majority communities. UNHCR published a report “Sustainability and reintegration challenges of returnees/IDPs” at the high-level event with all relevant stakeholders that highlighted progress and challenges in various fields ranging from legislative/institutional developments, access to rights and services, housing, access to health services, education rights, child protection, security, and socio-economic integration. The reports produced and the improvements promoted relate to the implementation of the of the law on allocation for use and exchange of municipal immovable property was produced with special focus on returnees and IDP’s; implementation of the legal framework on social housing, specifically Law on Housing Financing Specific Programs; implementation of the Regulation No. 01/2018 for the return of displaced persons and durable solutions.
In addition UNHCR provided commentaries to 10 legal acts or strategies:  Namely, concept documents were produced for laws on citizenship, civil status, and residence, relating to persons at risk of statelessness and stateless persons. Contributions relating to IDPs and returnees were provided for the Draft Law on Population and Housing Census; Draft MCR Strategy for Protection and Promotion of the Rights of the Communities and their Members; Draft Strategy on Rule of Law with special focus on access to rights, socio-economic integration, property issues and court proceedings; draft Law on Early Education for children of 0-6 years; draft amended Law on Free legal Aid; and draft Law on Local Self-Government.

children.description:
Agencies: UN Habitat; UNDP																		

UN-Habitat: UN-Habitat has been supporting the municipalities in Mitrovica Region in increasing environmental performance and climate responsiveness through spatial planning documents and their respective Strategic Environmental Assessments (SEAs), as well as Sustainable Urban Mobility Plans (SUMPs). SEAs provide analysis on environmental sustainability in spatial plans (including analysis on pollution levels, habitats of endangered species, flood zone susceptibility, land degradation, etc.) aiming to improve environmental protection, human health and quality of life, while reducing negative impacts of the measures foreseen in the respective plans and promoting sustainable development. Whereas SUMPs are sectorial plans designed to tackle transport-related problems in urban areas more efficiently and sustainably, which aim to improve and harmonize the needs of all traffic participants for free and safe movement within a functional urban area while enhancing living comfort, ensuring a better quality of life, and at the same time reducing transport-related emissions.

children.name: Strengthening institutional capacities of ministry responsible for environment, MAFRD and municipal authorities to plan for integrated, gender responsive, sustainable, and inclusive management of land and forestry resources
children.description:
Agencies: UN Habitat; FAO			

UN-Habitat: UN-Habitat has been supporting 7 municipalities in Mitrovica Region (including Mitrovica South, Mitrovica North, Vushtrri/Vucitrn and Skenderaj/Srbica, Zubin Potok, Zvecan and Leposavic) to develop integrated and participatory spatial planning documents, including Municipal Development Plans (MDPs) and Municipal Zoning Maps (MZMs). MDP is a multi-sectoral document that defines the long-term limits of economic, social and spatial development, whereas MZM determines in detail (through graphs, photos, maps and text) the type, destination, planned spatial use and action measures that are based on the duration and justifiable projections for public and private investment for all the territory of the municipality. COVID-19 lock down measures provided challenges for organizing meetings with municipal counterparts, citizens and other stakeholders regarding public consultations in Mitrovica Region, whereas local elections and related activities prolonged the approval of strategic development documents. Not all Municipal Planning Team members were trained and technically equipped to work remotely. Additional challenges remain in obtaining adequate data from institutions functioning in the Serbian system.
